In mathematics, more specifically in [[chromatic homotopy theory]], the '''redshift conjecture''' states, roughly, that [[algebraic K-theory]] <math>K(R)</math> has chromatic level one higher than that of a complex-oriented [[ring spectrum]] ''R''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Future directions |first=Tyler |last=Lawson |date=2013 |work=Talbot 2013: Chromatic Homotopy Theory |publisher=MIT Talbot Workshop |url=https://math.mit.edu/events/talbot/2013/19-Lawson-thefuture.pdf}}</ref>
It was formulated by John Rognes in a lecture at [[Schloss Ringberg]], Germany, in January 1999, and made more precise by him in a lecture at the [[Oberwolfach Research Institute for Mathematics]], Germany, in September 2000.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mn.uio.no/math/personer/vit/rognes/papers/red-shift.pdf |title=Algebraic K-theory of finitely presented ring spectra |first=John |last=Rognes |date=2000 |work=Oberwolfach talk }}</ref> In July 2022, Robert Burklund, [[Tomer Schlank]] and Allen Yuan announced a solution of a version of the redshift conjecture for arbitrary <math>E_{\infty}</math>-ring spectra, after Hahn and Wilson did so earlier in the case of the truncated Brown-Peterson spectra <math>BP\langle{n}\rangle</math>.<ref>Burklund, Schlank, Yuan (2022). ''The Chromatic Nullstellensatz''</ref>
